strongEvidence: identifies relevant players, roles, events, or triggers that were visible
names concrete observation windows rather than vague 'I watched'
separates what was seen from what it might mean
weakEvidence: lists hockey roles from memory without scene reference
outcome-only judgements ('they found him because they scored')

strongEvidence: describes functional relationships between players (support, cover, outlet)
ties role claims to visible positioning or actions
avoids inventing player intent
weakEvidence: confuses personal playing skill with reading roles

strongEvidence: identifies relevant spatial relationships (gaps, layers, width/depth)
references observable spacing or structure
connects spatial configuration to available possibilities without inventing intent
weakEvidence: unsupported tactical labels (system names as proof)

strongEvidence: names available options under stated conditions
identifies the chosen action distinctly from the result
links decision to visible constraints (time/space/pressure)
weakEvidence: praises or blames the outcome instead of the decision
claims 'always the right play' without options considered
invents what the player 'wanted' to do

strongEvidence: marks a visible change over time (before → after)
describes first reaction / follow-up sequence with anchors
scopes claims to the observed transition window
weakEvidence: static structure talk with no temporal change

strongEvidence: grounds pressure in visible cues (forecheck, gap, stick/body access)
relates pressure to restricted time/space/options
avoids equating scoreboard result with control quality
weakEvidence: system name as substitute for observed control
outcome bias (they lost control because they conceded)

strongEvidence: synthesizes recurring collective behaviour across comparable cases
keeps claims segment-scoped (not eternal team identity)
notes counterexamples or limits when present
separates observation from inference
matches claim strength to sample size / comparability
avoids unsupported causality; states limits
weakEvidence: hockey theory without reference to delivered observations
